summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end using GSD workflows — research, plan, verify, execute across 7 waves — then diagnose and close a gap discovered during final verification, while also spinning up a parallel worktree for independent Phase 69 work.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning (12 plans/7 waves) completed and executed cleanly with independent spot-checks at every wave, but final phase verification found the headline SC#5 desync bug was not actually fixed (ensureFolderLoaded cache short-circuit). A 2-plan gap-closure cycle (68.2-13, 68.2-14) was planned, plan-checked, and was executing plan 14 (final web wiring + desync e2e proof) when the transcript ends. A separate git worktree for Phase 69 was created off origin/main for parallel independent execution.

repo: gsd-tools commit helper can report `commit_failed` even when the commit landed successfully in git log — a known false negative, always verify with `git log` before treating it as a real failure.

Executors sometimes prematurely mark REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes `[x]` when only part of the acceptance criteria (e.g. code added but old services not yet deleted) is done; must be spot-checked and reverted until the full criteria (including deletions in later waves) are met.

The GSD planner can miss 'unowned' consumers of data structures being changed (e.g. 5+ components consuming SealedChildRef/ResolvedChild, and 15+ importers of modules slated for deletion vs the 5 the planner anticipated) — these surface only during execution and must be mapped via grep before destructive plans (deletions) run.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel executors require their own `pnpm install` per worktree — expensive — making sequential execution on the main tree preferable when most waves are single-plan.

`worktree.baseRef: 'head'` vs the 'fresh' default matters: executors forking from origin/main instead of HEAD would miss uncommitted PLAN.md files; always verify baseRef before dispatching worktree executors.
Web executors must rebuild the SDK dist before typecheck when SDK facade methods change, due to cross-package staleness (dist vs source) landmine.

grep-based acceptance criteria can pass while runtime behavior is still broken ('grep ACs pass, runtime fails') — e.g. D-03 freshness call sites were wired correctly but called into a `listFolder`/`ensureFolderLoaded` method that structurally couldn't re-resolve due to a self-referential sequenceNumber comparison.

code.finding: ensureFolderLoaded short-circuits on cached folderTree entries and never re-resolves IPNS on repeat navigation — root cause of the SC#5 owner/grantee desync bug.
ROT-07 enforceResolved gate added here for root folder resolve (plan 68.2-01).
ROT-07 enforceResolved gate added here in dfsFindFolder child loop (plan 68.2-01), alongside pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.

resolveChildren docstring documents that unverifiable siblings are gracefully skipped rather than rendered, since navigating into any child re-triggers the ROT-07 gate — an intentional availability/security tradeoff, not a vulnerability.
Gap-fix gated live-resolve (forceResolve) fails closed before any floor mutation, mirroring dfsFindFolder's gate exactly.
Gap-fix forceResolve path routes through enforceResolved so below-floor sequence numbers are still rejected.
In-flight dedup added for reresolveFolderInPlace to avoid duplicate concurrent re-resolves.

workflow: When pausing scheduled work mid-session, recompute delaySeconds from a freshly-fetched current time immediately before calling ScheduleWakeup — a delay computed earlier (before a quota interruption ate ~25 min) silently drifted the wake time by that same amount.

For security-critical or security-adjacent plan output (SDK read-path gates, crypto), independently re-run the acceptance tests/gates rather than trusting the executor's self-reported PASS, especially when the executor reports a 'deviation'.

Log discovered coverage gaps as todos immediately (matching repo's `.planning/todos/pending/` dated-markdown convention) even when the user chooses to proceed past a checker warning, so the gap isn't lost.
Before dispatching a plan that deletes shared modules, run a comprehensive residual-importer + boundary-violation audit rather than trusting the plan's originally-scoped file list.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper's `commit_failed` false negative required manual `git log` verification multiple times across the session.
Post-planning gap-analysis gate output contained control characters that broke the parser, requiring the check to be re-run directly instead of through the normal query path.
zsh glob syntax choked on an importer-mapping grep command, requiring a rewrite.

Session hit its usage quota mid-execution (between Wave 4 plan 04 and plan 06), forcing a pause; the first ScheduleWakeup attempt used a stale delay computed before the quota gap and would have resumed 25 minutes late (04:35 instead of 4:10am) — caught only because the user asked directly.
A stray/leftover scheduled wakeup (04:11) couldn't be cleanly retracted after the user said to skip the wait and resume immediately — had to be tolerated as a harmless future no-op.

`git fetch` failed in the sandboxed session (no network access), forcing reliance on a possibly-stale local origin/main ref when creating the Phase 69 worktree (verified acceptable only because it matched the 68.2 branch's known-current fork base).

Final phase verification revealed the phase's namesake bug (SC#5 desync) was never actually fixed despite all 12 plans executing cleanly and all unit/typecheck gates passing — a planner-level gap in behavioral coverage of the D-03 freshness legs.
